verdict.rationale: Adyen documents part of this story itself: webhooks for asynchronous status changes, and resultCode/refusalReason fields that describe unsuccessful payments, so an agent can monitor failed payments via API and webhooks. The pack has no first-party payment-retry or dunning capability. Idempotency covers safely retrying an API request, not re-attempting a declined charge, and the MCP tools cover sessions, payment links, refunds and cancels rather than retries. missing for 10: documented automatic or agent-driven failed-payment retry logic, dunning/customer outreach, failed-payment-specific webhook events, MCP tools for retry/dunning, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent monitor failed payments via API and webhooks and drive retries and dunning outreach

citations.quote: When the payment or modification request is unsuccessful, the `resultCode`, `refusalReason`, and `refusalReasonCode` describe the issue.
With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
In your Customer Area, you can find a log of all webhook events sent to your server.
